rationale: attr_struct_mismatch shows the strongest landmarker separation (p99 0.914 vs p50 0.314, std 0.245), and the profile pairs rich structure (modularity 0.519, clustering_coeff 0.533, degree_std 161.8, 26 communities) with low-dimensional template features (feature_dim 10), so attribute-based and structure-based rankings can genuinely diverge. conformity is directly indicated by feature_dup_rate 0.489 and feature_sparsity 0.480: a template-dominated feature matrix where anomalies can camouflage as feature-space in-liers, a mechanism none of the tail-outlier paradigms capture; its saturated score distribution (p50 0.870) is itself consistent with that template dominance rather than a counter-signal. homophily_violation is reliable because homophily is high (0.749), making feature-neighbor mismatch discriminative, and its landmarker has a clean upper tail (p99 0.841, mean 0.387). community contributes a distinct structural-adherence view backed by strong modularity (0.519) and clustering (0.533) over 26 communities. density is excluded because its landmarker is effectively dead (p90 and p95 both 0.0), and reconstruction/one-class are dropped as redundant and weak on a 10-dimensional template feature space already covered by the selected complementary views.

The graph is strongly homophilous (homophily=0.749) with dense neighborhoods (avg_degree=88.3), so neighbors are expected to agree and feature-neighbor mismatch is a natural anomaly signal; its landmarker confirms a separated upper tail (mean=0.387, p95=0.721, p99=0.841). attr_struct_mismatch has the cleanest tail separation of all landmarkers (mean=0.352 but p95=0.799, p99=0.914), indicating a distinct minority where attribute and structure rankings diverge, a complementary cross-modal view to the neighborhood-feature test. Community adherence is meaningful given modularity=0.519, 26 communities and high clustering_coeff=0.533, and its landmarker shows a poor-fit tail (p95=0.599, p99=0.734), adding a purely structural view. conformity is applicable because the feature matrix is template-dominated (feature_dup_rate=0.489, feature_dim=10): with anomalies plausibly hiding as feature-space in-liers, the negative-residual camouflage hypothesis is a genuinely complementary opposite to the outlier-oriented tests. I dropped local_affinity as redundant with homophily_violation (same neighbor-agreement mechanism, weaker tail p99=0.697), dropped density since its landmarker is dead (p90=p95=0, p99=0.048, no low-density regions), and left spectral out as its tail is the weakest of the surviving candidates (p95=0.416).

The graph is dense (avg_degree 88.28), highly clustered (clustering_coeff 0.533) and strongly assortative (homophily 0.749) with a modular community structure (modularity 0.519, 26 communities) and only feature_dim 10, so feature-only outlier views are weak and neighbor/structure-aware views are favoured. Among the label-free landmarkers, attr_struct_mismatch has the most sharply separated upper tail (p90 0.717, p95 0.799, p99 0.914, std 0.245), directly evidencing nodes whose attribute-based and structure-based rankings diverge; it leads. homophily_violation is next strongest (p99 0.841, mean 0.387) and is well-motivated by the high homophily (0.749) that makes feature-neighbor mismatch meaningful. conformity is selected on the template-dominated feature matrix (feature_dup_rate 0.489 >= 0.4, feature_sparsity 0.480, feature_dim 10): its saturated high scores (p50 0.870) confirm dominant-template features where anomalies hide as feature-space in-liers, a mechanism complementary to the outlier-style views above. community adds a distinct structural view justified by modularity 0.519 across 26 communities with a moderately separated tail (p99 0.734). Density is excluded (dead landmarker, p95 0.0), and local_affinity is dropped as redundant with homophily_violation, keeping the set complementary rather than overlapping.
